mainTopic: A שומר's claim that he returned a פקדון despite the owner's שטר, and the dispute and final ruling about a שטר כיס presented against יתומים
overview: This amud finishes a back-and-forth between רב עמרם and רב חסדא about a שומר who says he returned a פקדון while the owner still holds the שטר. רב חסדא explains that the שומר is believed, but only with a שבועה. The גמרא then suggests their argument matches an older dispute about a שטר כיס, a business-venture document, presented against יתומים. In that dispute דייני גולה say the investor swears and collects everything, and דייני ארץ ישראל say he swears and collects half. Both courts accept the rule of נהרדעי that an עיסקא is half מלוה and half פקדון. The גמרא rejects the match. Everyone agrees with רב חסדא, and the courts only argue whether a father who had paid would surely have told his children, or whether death may have stopped him. Two rulings of רב הונא בר אבין are then shown to fit together for that same reason. Finally, רבא rules that the investor collects half, מר זוטרא rules like דייני גולה, and רבינא challenges him. מר זוטרא's answer begins here and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Even a claim of forced loss needs an oath
steps.stepSummary: רב עמרם challenges רב חסדא: a שומר who says the item was lost by force must swear, so how can one who says 'I returned it' be believed without an oath?
steps.simpleTranslation: In the end, when the שומר tells the owner 'the items were taken by force,' doesn't he need to swear?
steps.whatsHappening: רב עמרם pushes back on רב חסדא's claim that the שומר is believed when he says he returned the deposit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even the normal, believable claim of נאנסו only works together with a שבועה. So saying the שומר is simply 'believed' about returning the item seems too generous. At the very least he should need an oath.

keyTerms.meaning: in the end, ultimately
they were lost through forces beyond his control
an oath
needs, requires

phrases.english: Ultimately,
when he says to him, 'They were taken by force,'
phrases.notes: This is רב עמרם speaking to רב חסדא. The 'he' is the שומר who was holding the deposit.

phrases.english: doesn't he need an oath?

steps.triggerLanguage: סוֹף סוֹף, כִּי אָמַר לֵיהּ ״נֶאֶנְסוּ״, לָאו שְׁבוּעָה בָּעֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier exchange in which רב חסדא ruled that the שומר is believed.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's statement that the שומר is believed to say he returned the פקדון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A claim of נאנסו, which the law accepts, still needs a שבועה. So a claim of returning the item cannot be accepted with no oath at all.

steps.title: Believed means believed with an oath
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא explains that by 'believed' he meant believed together with a שבועה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, what did I mean by 'believed'? Believed with an oath.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers that he never meant the שומר goes free without swearing. He meant the שומר is believed once he swears.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer narrows what 'believed' means without giving up the main point. The owner's holding the שטר does not cancel the שומר's claim. The שומר is still handled like any שומר, with a שבועה.

keyTerms.meaning: here too, in this case as well
believed, trusted
with an oath

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב חסדא, a שומר who says he returned a פקדון is believed with a שבועה, even though the owner still holds the document.

phrases.english: Here too,
what did 'believed' mean?
believed with an oath.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב עמרם's challenge by clarifying the meaning of 'believed'.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifying the meaning of a word
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought 'believed' meant believed without any oath.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Believed' means believed together with a שבועה, like any other claim of a שומר.

steps.title: Suggesting the argument matches a dispute of תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רב עמרם and רב חסדא disagree about the same point as a ברייתא dispute about a שטר כיס presented against יתומים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this matches the dispute of these תנאים? A ברייתא teaches: when a purse document is presented against orphans, דייני גולה say the lender swears and collects all of it, and דייני ארץ ישראל say he swears and collects half.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a comparison. It brings an older dispute and will soon try to show that it is the same argument as רב עמרם and רב חסדא's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שטר כיס records money handed over for a joint business venture. Here the person who received the money died, and the investor wants to collect from his יתומים. Both courts require a שבועה, but they disagree on whether he collects all of the money or only half.

keyTerms.meaning: shall we say? A word that introduces a suggestion
תנאים, the sages of the משנה and ברייתא era
a 'purse document' recording money given for a joint business venture
orphans, here the heirs of the one who received the money
the judges of the exile, meaning בבל

phrases.english: Shall we say they argue about the dispute of these תנאים?
As it is taught in a ברייתא:
A purse document that comes out against the orphans:
phrases.notes: The investor brings the venture document to collect from the heirs of the man who took the money.

phrases.english: The judges of the exile say:
He swears and collects all of it.
And the judges of Eretz Yisrael say:
He swears and collects half.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the רב עמרם and רב חסדא dispute is settled, the גמרא looks for an earlier source with the same argument.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the רב עמרם and רב חסדא argument already a dispute between תנאים?

steps.title: Everyone agrees with נהרדעי: half loan, half deposit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא assumes both courts accept the rule of נהרדעי that an עיסקא is half מלוה and half פקדון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Everyone holds like נהרדעי, who say: this business venture is half a loan and half a deposit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a shared starting point that both courts agree on. This prepares the way to explain exactly where they differ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Half of the money in an עיסקא counts as a loan, which the receiver must always pay back, so both courts let the investor collect that half. The other half counts as a deposit. The whole dispute must therefore be about that deposit half.

keyTerms.meaning: everyone agrees
the sages of the city נהרדעא
a business venture: money given to another person to trade with, and profits shared
a loan, which must be repaid no matter what
a deposit held for its owner

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the two courts disagree about the whole sum. They both let the investor collect the loan half; their argument is only about the deposit half.

phrases.english: And everyone holds like the sages of נהרדעא,
as the sages of נהרדעא say:
This business venture
is half a loan and half a deposit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the ברייתא dispute down to the deposit half of the money.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An עיסקא is half מלוה and half פקדון, and both courts accept this.

steps.title: Linking the dispute to 'What is your document doing in my hand?'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proposes that דייני גולה hold like רב עמרם and דייני ארץ ישראל hold like רב חסדא about the deposit half.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't this what they argue about? One Sage holds the owner can say, 'What is your document doing in my hand?' The other Sage holds we do not say this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its suggestion. The two courts' argument over the deposit half is the same as the argument between רב עמרם and רב חסדא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דייני גולה let the investor collect everything. That means the heirs are not believed to say the deposit half was returned, because the investor still holds the document, like רב עמרם. דייני ארץ ישראל give only half, so the father would have been believed about the deposit half despite the document, like רב חסדא.

keyTerms.meaning: what, isn't it...? Introduces a proposed explanation
they disagree
one Sage holds
'What is your document doing in my hand?' This is the owner's argument that the item was never returned.

steps.whyThisMatters: If this suggestion holds, the argument between רב עמרם and רב חסדא would be an old argument between תנאים, not something new.

phrases.english: What, isn't it in this that they disagree?
One Sage holds that he can say to him:
phrases.notes: This is the investor, who still holds the document, arguing against the claim that the deposit half was returned.

phrases.english: 'What is your document doing in my hand?'
And the other Sage holds that we do not say this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the shared rule of נהרדעי to place the courts' argument on the deposit half, then connects it to רב עמרם and רב חסדא.
steps.raayaObject: That the רב עמרם and רב חסדא argument is the same as the argument between דייני גולה and דייני ארץ ישראל
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of the שטר כיס presented against יתומים, read together with the rule of נהרדעי

steps.title: Everyone agrees with רב חסדא; the real argument is whether the father would have told his children
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion from step 5. Both courts hold like רב חסדא. They argue whether a father who paid back would surely have told his children, or whether death may have stopped him.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Everyone holds like רב חסדא. Here they argue about this: one side says that if the father had really paid it back, he would have said so. The other side says: maybe the Angel of Death stopped him from saying it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the idea that the two courts argue about רב חסדא's rule. It gives a new reason for their argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both courts agree that a שומר who says 'I returned it' is believed. So the argument is not about that rule. דייני גולה say the father's silence proves he never paid back the deposit half, so the lender collects everything. דייני ארץ ישראל say he may simply have died before he could tell anyone, so the court protects the orphans on the deposit half, and the lender collects only half.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone; all opinions agree
They argue about
If it were true that he paid it back
The Angel of Death
Forced him, stopped him against his will

steps.confusionAlert: The one who 'paid back' and 'would have said so' is the dead father (the borrower), not the lender. The question is whether his silence to his children means anything.

phrases.english: No; for everyone
holds the view of רב חסדא;
phrases.notes: Both courts agree that a שומר who says 'I gave it back' is believed (steps 1-2).

phrases.english: and here they argue about this:
one master holds:
if it were true that he paid it back,
he would surely have said so.
And the other master holds:
say that the Angel of Death
is what stopped him.
phrases.notes: He means the father died before he had a chance to tell his children.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא; דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא אִית לְהוּ דְּרַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 5's proposal and gives a new reason for the courts' argument.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that the courts argue about רב עמרם vs. רב חסדא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Both courts can accept רב חסדא. They argue about whether the father's silence shows he never paid.

steps.title: רב הונא בר אבין sends two rulings
steps.stepSummary: A שומר who says 'I returned it' is believed even though the depositor holds a document. But a lender with a שטר כיס against orphans swears and collects everything.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר אבין sent this message: If someone deposits something with a friend and has a document, and the friend says 'I gave it back to you,' he is believed. And a שטר כיס that is brought against orphans: the lender swears and collects all of it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement is brought. רב הונא בר אבין gives two rulings side by side, and they will soon seem to clash.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ruling matches רב חסדא: a שומר is believed when he says he returned the item, even if the depositor holds a document. The second ruling matches דייני גולה: the lender collects the whole שטר כיס from the orphans after an oath.

keyTerms.meaning: One who deposits an item with someone
With a written document
I returned it to you
A 'purse document' recording a joint business deal (עיסקא)
Swears and collects all of it

phrases.english: רב הונא בר אבין sent:
One who deposits with his friend with a document,
and he says to him: 'I returned it to you' —
he is believed.
And a purse document brought against the orphans —
he swears and collects all of it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a related ruling that fits the explanation in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שומר is believed to say he returned a deposit, even if there is a document. A שטר כיס against orphans is collected in full after an oath.

steps.title: Don't the two rulings contradict each other?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how both rulings can be true together.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two rulings?! (They seem to contradict each other.)
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב הונא בר אבין's two rulings because they seem to clash.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a שומר is believed to say 'I returned it,' then the court should make that claim for the orphans on the deposit half of the שטר כיס. So the lender should not collect all of it.

keyTerms.meaning: Two (here: two rulings that seem to clash)

phrases.english: Two?!
phrases.notes: He means: how can both rulings stand together? They seem to point opposite ways.

steps.kashyaTarget: The two rulings of רב הונא בר אבין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the 'I returned it' claim works, the court should make it for the orphans, so the lender should not collect everything.

steps.title: The orphans' case is different: the father would have told them
steps.stepSummary: With the orphans, if the father had paid, he would have told them. So no claim of payment is made for them.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there: if he had really paid it back, he would surely have said so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge, using the same reasoning as דייני גולה from step 6.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A living שומר can say for himself 'I returned it.' A dead father did not say it, and his silence shows he never paid. So the court does not make that claim for the orphans.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different there
He would surely have said so

phrases.english: It is different there,
phrases.notes: 'There' is the שטר כיס against orphans.

phrases.english: for if it were true that he paid it back —
he would surely have said so.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: The court should claim payment for the orphans just as a שומר can claim it for himself.
steps.terutzMaskana: The father's silence shows he did not pay, so no such claim is made for the orphans.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that רב הונא בר אבין holds both רב חסדא's rule and the view of דייני גולה, just as step 6 explained.

steps.title: רבא rules: swear and collect half
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules like דייני ארץ ישראל: the lender swears and collects half.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The הלכה is that he swears and collects half.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the practical הלכה in the שטר כיס case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Collecting half matches דייני ארץ ישראל. The lender collects the loan half. On the deposit half, the court protects the orphans, since maybe the father died before telling them.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law is
Collects half

phrases.english: רבא said: The הלכה is —
he swears and collects half.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from explaining the argument to deciding it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The lender with a שטר כיס against orphans swears and collects half, like דייני ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: מר זוטרא rules like דייני גולה
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא rules like דייני גולה, which seems to mean the lender collects all of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא said: The הלכה follows דייני גולה.
steps.whatsHappening: A later חכם gives a ruling that seems to go against רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At first glance, ruling like דייני גולה means the lender swears and collects the whole sum. That is how רבינא understands it, but מר זוטרא's answer (step 13) begins to explain his own version of דייני גולה's view. This seems to clash with רבא's ruling of half.

keyTerms.meaning: The judges of the exile (בבל)

phrases.english: מר זוטרא said:
The הלכה follows the judges of the exile.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר זוּטְרָא: הִלְכְתָא כְּדַיָּינֵי גוֹלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a ruling that seems to oppose רבא's.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows דייני גולה: at first glance this means the lender collects all of it, as רבינא assumes. מר זוטרא's own explanation follows in step 13.

steps.title: רבינא challenges מר זוטרא from רבא's ruling
steps.stepSummary: רבינא asks מר זוטרא: didn't רבא rule that he collects only half?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to מר זוטרא: But רבא said that he swears and collects half!
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא challenges מר זוטרא by pointing to רבא's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא ruled 'half,' like דייני ארץ ישראל. So how can מר זוטרא rule like דייני גולה, who say 'all'?

keyTerms.meaning: But he said! (pointing to a clashing source)

phrases.english: רבינא said to מר זוטרא,
but רבא said:
he swears and collects half!

steps.kashyaTarget: מר זוטרא's ruling like דייני גולה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא already ruled 'collect half,' which goes against דייני גולה.

steps.title: מר זוטרא begins his answer
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא starts to explain how he understands the view of דייני גולה. His answer continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: We, regarding the view of דייני גולה...
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא starts answering רבינא's challenge. His sentence continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He is about to explain how he received the view of דייני גולה. That explanation will show that his ruling does not really clash with רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: We

phrases.english: He said to him:
we, regarding that of the judges of the exile,
phrases.notes: The sentence isn't finished here. מר זוטרא keeps talking on the next amud.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifying the version of דייני גולה's view (continues on the next amud)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: מר זוטרא's ruling clashes with רבא's.
steps.terutzMaskana: The answer is completed on the next amud.
